title: security: any user who may import can send runAutomations: false and skip every trigger and metadata-bound hook, so a sales rep bypasses an approval gate and a closed-record freeze through POST /data/:object/import
body:
**P0 suspect (security):** an unprivileged caller can switch off the automation layer that enforces approvals and record freezes. Grade: triage's. Filed by the `repo:hotcrm` seat (`os-project-manager`, session `session_01BDgipbNowaGa139em8Fhoq`) from the hotcrm#2129 Target 1 os-dev report (PR objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2166), `class: a`. ⛔ Not a claim.

## What happens

**Measured, detail withheld pending maintainer.** The maintainer's disclosure ruling (2026-08-18, recorded on objectstack-ai/objectstack#9387) says no reproduction for an authentication or authorization hole is published anywhere on GitHub. A non-administrator who may import was measured, on `18.0.0-next.3`, to get a write past two app business controls through this door: an approval flow, and a closed-record freeze hook that refuses the same change through `PATCH`. The reproduction stays with the filing seat and the maintainer. Redacted by the triage seat at first grade; earlier revisions remain in this card's edit history, which only a repository admin can delete.

## Where (read on objectstack `origin/main`)

- `packages/rest/src/import-prepare.ts` around line 296: `const runAutomations = body?.runAutomations !== false;`. The value is read straight from the request body.
- `packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts` around line 758: `skipAutomations: !runAutomations` goes into the write context. `skipAutomations` implies `skipTriggers` and skips every metadata-bound hook (#22070 measured the same reach for the audit stamp).
- The route's only gate is `enforceApiAccess` on the object's enable flags. Nothing checks who may opt out.

## Governing text

- An app's approval flows and freeze hooks are its declared business controls. objectstack-ai/objectstack#22310 (closed, p0) states the rule for the sibling door: "an elevated sub-flow is an elevated door for everyone". This is the same shape: a caller-chosen flag that removes the controls.
- `packages/spec/src/api/export.zod.ts` around line 287 documents `runAutomations` as the way to get "a silent bulk load". A bulk-load opt-out is a migration capability. It should not be a right of every user who may import.

## Expected

The opt-out is honoured only for a caller entitled to it, for example `isSystem`, an administrator, or a declared permission. For anyone else it is refused loudly (403) or ignored, so automations run. Pin it with a non-admin caller on both legs above.

**Adjacent, unmeasured:** a second body flag read the same way, in the same file. The import door's fix measures it in the same round, and the detail is with the maintainer.

## Consumer note

HotCRM's dev-only `scripts/demo-staff.ts` (PR objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2166) uses this door as the **dev admin**, to hand demo deals to reps without opening approvals. A fix that keeps the opt-out for administrators changes nothing there. A fix that removes it entirely makes that script exit 1 by its own submitter check, which is the intended loud failure.

## Dedupe

objectstack issues were searched for "import runAutomations false non-admin bypass triggers hooks approval privilege skipAutomations". The near hits are objectstack-ai/objectstack#22310 (the `/automation/:name/trigger` door, closed), objectstack-ai/objectstack#22070 (the audit stamp skipped by `skipAutomations`, closed), objectstack-ai/objectstack#21848 and objectstack-ai/objectstack#3801. None covers who may send the import opt-out.
